# Run the nightshift daemon with its API and hub credentials

## Intent

nightshift is the process that owns a project's work on a Parley hub, and a
person steers it through an API. Before it can drive any work it has to
exist as a daemon a person can start, trust and ask: `nightshiftd` starts
only when its configuration, the hub and its two hub credentials are in
order, serves an authenticated HTTP API with a status and a resumable event
stream to the `nightshift` client, keeps running through a hub outage, and
stops cleanly on a signal.

## Goals

- **A daemon that refuses to start half-configured.** `nightshiftd` checks
  its configuration, the hub and the two credentials in that order, and a
  failed check ends it with exit code 1 and one line naming the check and
  the reason.
- **Two credentials with separate powers.** The worker token cannot approve
  and the approver token is another token; a start with anything else is
  refused.
- **Only the person's client reaches the API.** Every request under
  `/api/v1` carries the client token the daemon wrote at its first start.
- **A status a person can read.** `GET /api/v1/status` and `nightshift
  status` report the version, the hub's endpoint and whether it is
  reachable.
- **An event stream a client can resume.** `GET /api/v1/events` delivers
  every event with an increasing `seq`, replays from `Last-Event-ID`, and
  says `410 cursor_expired` when the cursor is older than what is kept (7
  days).
- **It survives a hub outage and a restart.** While the hub is unreachable
  the daemon keeps running, tries again every 30 seconds and continues by
  itself; events and their `seq` survive a restart.
- **It stops cleanly.** On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` it exits with code 0
  within 30 seconds.

## Non-goals

This package is the first of ten written from
`docs/prd/02-drive-work-items-through-the-hub.md`. The other scopes are
packages of their own, implemented in this order:

- **`02_workspaces_and_policy`**: `nightshift workspace …`, the policy
  commands, the states `green`, `red` and `held`, and the `workspaces`
  member of the status.
- **`03_work_items_and_inbox`**: work items, threads, decisions, the inbox
  routes and commands, `nightshift watch`, the notification command, and the
  `Unread` entries this PRD names for the hub's outage and for a token the
  hub stopped accepting. This package only keeps the facts those entries
  are written from.
- **`04_sessions_and_scheduling`**: the roles and the start checks `roles`
  and `sessions`, the session user, a session's own hub token, ending and
  recording sessions at shutdown, the `sessions` member of the status,
  scheduling, the daily limit and pausing.
- **`05_planning`**, **`06_implementation_and_review`**, **`07_landing`**,
  **`08_health_and_publishing`**, **`09_notes_and_take_over`**,
  **`10_rules_brief_and_forge`**.

Also out, for every package of that PRD: hosting code, landing or policy
(Parley's), working without a hub, a web or desktop client, an MCP facade,
and a team of several people.

No event is produced by this package itself: the stream carries the changes
of threads, decisions and work items, and the first of those arrive with
package 03. This package offers the log they are appended to.

## Background

The repository holds its `README.md`, the agent instructions, the steering
and two PRDs. There is no Go module, no `Makefile` and no code: every
command, route, file and package this document names is new.

Parley (`agent-fox-dev/parley`) is the hub. What this package uses of it,
as its `docs/api.md` states at commit `7eabfb9`:

- `GET /readyz` needs no credential and answers `200` when the hub can do
  its work.
- A personal access token (PAT) has the form
  `parley_pat_<token_id>_<secret>` and carries scopes in `permissions`.
  `GET /api/v1/user/tokens/{token_id}` answers the Token object of one of
  the caller's own tokens (`permissions`, `workspace`, `expires_at`,
  `revoked_at`) and needs the scope `tokens:read`, which `tokens:manage`
  satisfies.
- The hub checks a credential before a scope: a request with a token it
  does not accept is `401 unauthenticated`; one with an accepted token that
  lacks the route's scope is `403 insufficient_scope`; one with a token
  bound to a workspace on a route under `/api/v1/user` is `403
  token_bound`.

The stream follows Parley's own event cursor and Pizza Bot's inbox
(`github.com/agent-fox-dev/pizza-bot`): thin clients over HTTP and
server-sent events, with work that goes on when no client is connected.

## Requirements

Constraint: Linux and macOS; Windows is best effort. Constraint: Go, built
as two programs, `nightshiftd` (the daemon) and `nightshift` (the client),
which speaks only the daemon's HTTP API. Constraint: `nightshiftd` is one
process holding the controller, its store and the API.

### Configuration and start

`nightshiftd` reads one configuration file, `~/.nightshift/config.toml`
unless `--config` names another. In this package it holds:

| Key | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `listen` | the address the API listens on | `127.0.0.1:7878` |
| `token_file` | where the client token is kept | `~/.nightshift/token` |
| `[store].path` | the daemon's store, one SQLite file | `~/.nightshift/store.db` |
| `[hub].endpoint` | the hub's base URL | none, required |
| `[hub].worker_token` | the worker token | none, required |
| `[hub].approver_token` | the approver token | none, required |

A leading `~/` in a path is the home directory of the daemon's user.

At start it checks, in this order, that the configuration loads
(`config`), that the hub answers (`hub`) and that the credentials are
accepted and fit their purpose (`credentials`). A check that fails ends the
process with exit code 1 and one line on stderr naming the check and the
reason; no later check runs and nothing is started: no listener, no store,
no token file.

- `config` fails when the file is missing or unreadable, is not valid TOML,
  holds a key the daemon does not know (`config: unknown key
  "hub.endpont"`), or lacks a required key (`config: hub.endpoint is not
  set`).
- `hub` fails when `GET <endpoint>/readyz` does not answer `200` within 10
  seconds: `hub: connection refused` for a refused connection, `hub: readyz
  answered 503` for another status, `hub: timeout` for no answer.

After the checks the daemon opens its store, writes the client token where
none exists, and listens. A store that cannot be opened, a token file that
cannot be written or an address that cannot be bound ends the process the
same way (`store: …`, `token: …`, `listen: …`).

### Credentials

The configuration holds two personal access tokens of the person's Parley
account, which the person mints on the hub:

- the **worker token**, which nightshift uses for everything it does
  itself. It holds the scopes `workspaces:write`, `git:write`, `git:read`,
  `changes:write`, `checks:write`, `tokens:manage`, `forge:write`,
  `sessions:write` and `audit:read`, and is not bound to a workspace;
- the **approver token**, which nightshift uses only to record the person's
  verdict when they answer an `approval` decision. It holds `changes:read`
  and `changes:approve`.

The start check `credentials` fails, with these reasons after
`credentials: `:

- a token is not of the form `parley_pat_<token_id>_<secret>` (`worker
  token is not a personal access token`);
- the two are the same token (`worker and approver are the same token`);
- the hub answers either token `401` (`worker token: 401 unauthenticated`);
- the worker token is bound to a workspace (`worker token is bound to a
  workspace`);
- the worker token holds `changes:approve` (`worker token must not hold
  changes:approve`);
- a token lacks a scope named above, by its exact name in the token's
  `permissions` (`worker token lacks checks:write`); the first missing one
  in the order above is named.

A token that the hub stops accepting while the daemon runs (expired or
revoked: the hub answers it `401`) is treated as the hub being unreachable
for what needs that token, and `status` names it (`worker token: 401
unauthenticated`). The daemon reads the configuration's credentials again
when it receives `SIGHUP` and runs the `credentials` check on them: tokens
that pass replace the ones in use and clear the reported error; tokens that
fail are not taken, the ones in use stay, and the reason is written to the
daemon's log.

### The client token and the API

On its first start the daemon writes a client token, 64 hexadecimal
characters from 32 random bytes, to the token file, readable and writable
by its owner only (mode `0600`). A later start keeps the token it finds.

The API lives under `/api/v1` and answers JSON. Every request carries the
client token as a bearer token; without it, or with another, the answer is
`401` with `error_type: unauthorized`, before the route is looked at. An
error is `{"error_type", "message"}` with a 4xx or 5xx status: `404
not_found` for a path that names no route, `405 method_not_allowed` for a
method the route does not have.

### Status

`GET /api/v1/status` reports:

```json
{"version": "dev",
 "hub": {"endpoint": "https://hub.example", "reachable": true,
         "unreachable_since": null, "credential_error": null},
 "sessions": [],
 "workspaces": []}
```

`sessions` and `workspaces` are empty lists in this package; packages 04
and 02 fill them.

`nightshift status` prints it for a terminal:

```text
nightshiftd dev
hub: https://hub.example reachable
```

with `hub: unreachable since <time>` on the second line while the hub is
unreachable, and a third line `<credential_error>` when there is one. With
`--json` it prints the API's JSON.

The client finds the daemon at `--addr`, else at `$NIGHTSHIFT_ADDR`, else
at `127.0.0.1:7878`, and reads the client token from `--token-file`, else
from `~/.nightshift/token`. Exit codes of every `nightshift` command: 0 on
success; 1 when the daemon refuses (the error's `message` on stderr) or
cannot be reached (`cannot reach nightshiftd at <address>`), or the token
file cannot be read (`cannot read the client token at <path>`); 2 for a
usage error (an unknown command or flag, a missing argument), with the
usage on stderr and no request sent.

### The event stream

The daemon keeps an event log in its store. An event has a `seq`, one
greater than the event before it and starting at 1, a `time`, a `type` and
a `data` object; the packages that produce events define their types.

`GET /api/v1/events` is a server-sent event stream: each event is sent as
`id: <seq>`, `event: <type>` and `data: <the event as JSON>`. A client that
connects without `Last-Event-ID` receives the events appended from then on.
A client that connects with `Last-Event-ID: <seq>` first receives every
event after that `seq`, in order, then the new ones, none missing and none
twice.

Events are kept for 7 days. When an event after the given `seq` is no
longer kept, the answer is `410` with `error_type: cursor_expired` and the
member `oldest_seq`. A `Last-Event-ID` that is not a non-negative integer,
or is greater than the newest `seq`, is `400` with `error_type:
invalid_request`.

A client that does not read falls behind: when 256 events wait for it, the
daemon closes its connection, and the client reconnects with its last
`seq`. Appending an event never waits for a client.

The log survives a restart: after it, `seq` goes on from the highest value
ever given, and a client that reconnects with its last `seq` receives what
it missed.

### Stopping, and the hub's outages

On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT` the daemon stops accepting requests, closes the
event streams, runs the steps other packages registered for a shutdown
(package 04 ends its sessions there), closes the store and exits with code
0 within 30 seconds. A step that has not returned 25 seconds after the
signal is abandoned; the daemon exits with code 0 all the same.

**When the hub is unreachable** (a request to it fails with a connection
error or a timeout, or `/readyz` does not answer `200`), the daemon keeps
running. `status` reports `hub: unreachable` with the time of the first
failure. The daemon asks `/readyz` again every 30 seconds and continues by
itself when it answers `200`. Until then it answers "not available" to any
part of nightshift that asks whether work needing the hub may start, which
is how later packages start no session and land nothing meanwhile.

### End-to-end flows

**A first start and a status query.** The person writes a configuration and
starts `nightshiftd`. It reads the file, asks the hub's `/readyz`, reads
both tokens' scopes from the hub, opens the store, writes
`~/.nightshift/token` and listens. The person runs `nightshift status` and
reads the version and `hub: … reachable`.

**A client resumes the event stream after a restart.** A client is
connected to `/api/v1/events` and has received events up to a `seq`.
`nightshiftd` receives `SIGTERM` and exits with code 0. More events are
appended after the next start. The client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`
and receives every event after its `seq`.

**The hub goes away and comes back.** The hub stops answering. The daemon
marks it unreachable; `nightshift status` prints `hub: unreachable since
<time>`. The hub answers again; at its next probe the daemon marks it
reachable and `nightshift status` prints `hub: … reachable`, with no
restart.

## Design Decisions

1. **Two personal access tokens, a worker and an approver, instead of the
   owner's API key.** The owner decided it (decision 8 of the source PRD).
2. **API and command-line client in version 1; one daemon, one person.**
   The owner decided it (decision 21 of the source PRD).
3. **This package is the first of ten.** The owner agreed to the split on
   2026-11-28: the source PRD's decision 32 with sessions ahead of planning
   and notes and taking over behind landing.
4. **The start checks `roles` and `sessions` belong to package 04.**
   Chosen here: they check the roles and the session user, which that
   package introduces; it adds them to the sequence after `credentials`.
5. **The hub "answers" when `GET /readyz` is `200` within 10 seconds.**
   Chosen here: it needs no credential, so the `hub` check does not
   overlap the `credentials` check.
6. **A token's scopes are read with the worker token from `GET
   /api/v1/user/tokens/{token_id}`; the approver token is accepted when the
   hub answers it anything but `401` on that route.** Chosen here: the
   approver token holds no scope that reads tokens, and the hub checks the
   credential before the scope.
7. **Scopes are compared by exact name.** Chosen here: the source PRD
   names the scopes each token holds, and the hub's own subset rule for
   minting counts exact names only.
8. **A token that is not a PAT, and a worker token bound to a workspace,
   fail the `credentials` check.** Chosen here: the source PRD requires
   both properties and names no reason for them.
9. **Credentials that fail the check at `SIGHUP` are not taken.** Chosen
   here: a daemon that is running should not lose working credentials to a
   typo.
10. **An unknown configuration key fails the `config` check.** Chosen here:
    a misspelled limit would otherwise be ignored silently.
11. **The store is one SQLite file, `~/.nightshift/store.db` unless
    configured, through `modernc.org/sqlite`.** Chosen here: one process,
    one person, no server to run; Parley uses the same driver.
12. **`token_file` is a configuration key.** Chosen here: a daemon started
    with `--config` elsewhere, and every test, needs the token somewhere
    other than the home directory.
13. **The client takes the daemon's address from `--addr` or
    `$NIGHTSHIFT_ADDR`, and does not read the daemon's configuration.**
    Chosen here: the configuration holds the hub credentials, which the
    client has no need to read.
14. **The API checks the client token before the route.** Chosen here: a
    caller without the token learns nothing about which routes exist.
15. **A stream without `Last-Event-ID` starts at the present.** Chosen
    here: a client that wants the past reads the threads; one that wants a
    replay sends a cursor.
16. **A client 256 events behind is disconnected.** Chosen here: appending
    an event must never wait for a reader, and a reconnect with the cursor
    loses nothing.
17. **Shutdown steps are abandoned 25 seconds after the signal.** Chosen
    here: it leaves 5 seconds to close the store inside the 30 the source
    PRD allows.
18. **Command lines are parsed with the standard library's `flag`
    package.** Chosen here: the steering prefers the standard library, and
    the client's commands are a fixed table.
20. **The worker token also holds `git:read`, which the source PRD does not
    list.** Chosen here: the hub lets a PAT mint only scopes it holds by
    exact name, and nightshift mints the reviewer's session token with
    `git:read` (package 04). Without it every review would fail.
19. **The `Unread` entries for an outage of 15 minutes and for a token the
    hub stopped accepting are written by package 03.** Chosen here:
    threads are that package's; this one keeps the time of the first
    failure and the credential error they are written from.

## Glossary

- **hub**: a Parley server (`parleyd`).
- **worker token, approver token**: the two Parley personal access tokens
  nightshift holds: one for its own actions, one for the person's
  approvals.
- **client token**: the secret `nightshiftd` writes at its first start and
  the `nightshift` client sends with every request.
- **start check**: one of the named checks `nightshiftd` runs before it
  starts anything; a failure ends the process.
- **event**: one entry of the daemon's event log, with a `seq`, a `time`, a
  `type` and `data`.
- **cursor**: the `seq` a client sends as `Last-Event-ID` to receive the
  events after it.
- **store**: the daemon's SQLite file.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Configuration and start checks

**Rationale:** A daemon that starts half-configured fails later, in the middle of someone's work, with a worse message.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN nightshiftd is started, THE nightshiftd SHALL read its configuration from the file `--config` names, or from `~/.nightshift/config.toml` when the flag is absent, expanding a leading `~/` of every path value to the home directory of the daemon's user
   → the loaded configuration holds `listen`, `token_file`, `store.path`, `hub.endpoint`, `hub.worker_token` and `hub.approver_token` as the file gives them
   Check: unit
   - setup: a temporary home directory given to the loader as a parameter, not through the process environment
   ```
   new file internal/config/config_test.go, a table over {no flag -> <home>/.nightshift/config.toml is read, --config <path> -> <path> is read}: cfg = config.Load(path, home); assert every key equals the file's value; assert a store.path of '~/x.db' loads as <home>/x.db
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any key among `listen`, `token_file` and `store.path` that the configuration file omits, use the default `127.0.0.1:7878`, `~/.nightshift/token` and `~/.nightshift/store.db` respectively
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/config_test.go: cfg = config.Load(file with only the three [hub] keys, home); assert cfg.Listen == '127.0.0.1:7878'; assert cfg.TokenFile == home + '/.nightshift/token'; assert cfg.Store.Path == home + '/.nightshift/store.db'
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF the configuration file is missing or unreadable, is not valid TOML, holds a key nightshiftd does not know, or lacks `hub.endpoint`, `hub.worker_token` or `hub.approver_token`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `config` and start nothing
   → exit code 1; exactly one line on stderr, `config: <reason>`, where the reason names the file for a missing or malformed one, is `unknown key "<dotted key>"` for an unknown key and `<dotted key> is not set` for a missing one; no request is sent to the hub, no listener is opened, and neither the token file nor the store file is created
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/config_test.go, a table over {missing file, 'listen = ' (malformed), 'hub.endpont' present, each of the three required keys absent}: _, err = config.Load(path, home); assert err.Error() == the expected reason. In internal/daemon/start_test.go: code, stderr = daemon.Run(args with a config lacking hub.endpoint); assert code == 1; assert stderr == 'config: hub.endpoint is not set\n'; assert the fake hub saw no request; assert token file and store file do not exist
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN nightshiftd is started, THE nightshiftd SHALL run the start checks in the order `config`, `hub`, `credentials`, and run no check after the first one that fails
   → on a failure: exit code 1 and exactly one line on stderr that begins with the failed check's name and a colon
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) whose /readyz answers 503 and which answers every token 401
   ```
   in internal/daemon/start_test.go: code, stderr = daemon.Run(valid config pointing at the fake hub); assert code == 1; assert stderr has one line and it starts with 'hub: '; assert the fake hub saw no request under /api/v1
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF `GET <hub.endpoint>/readyz` is not answered with status 200 within 10 seconds, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `hub` and start nothing
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `hub: connection refused` for a refused connection, `hub: readyz answered <status>` for another status, `hub: timeout` when no answer came within 10 seconds; no listener is opened and neither the token file nor the store file is created
   Check: integration
   - setup: the check's timeout is a parameter the test sets to 50 milliseconds for the timeout case
   ```
   in internal/daemon/start_test.go, a table over {endpoint of a closed listener -> 'hub: connection refused', fake hub with readyz 503 -> 'hub: readyz answered 503', fake hub that never answers -> 'hub: timeout'}: code, stderr = daemon.Run(cfg); assert code == 1; assert stderr == want + '\n'; assert no token file, no store file
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] WHEN every start check passed, THE nightshiftd SHALL open the store at `store.path`, creating the file and its parent directory where they do not exist, and serve the API on the `listen` address
   → the process keeps running; `GET /api/v1/status` on the listen address with the client token answers 200
   Check: same as PATH-1
1. [REQ-1.7] IF after the start checks passed, the store cannot be opened, the client token file cannot be written, or the listen address cannot be bound, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL end the process without serving the API
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr, `store: <error>`, `token: <error>` or `listen: <error>`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub that passes the hub and credentials checks
   ```
   in internal/daemon/start_test.go, a table over {store.path inside a file that is not a directory -> prefix 'store: ', token_file inside a read-only directory -> prefix 'token: ', listen on an address a test listener already holds -> prefix 'listen: '}: code, stderr = daemon.Run(cfg); assert code == 1; assert stderr is one line with the prefix
   ```

### REQ-2: Hub credentials

**Rationale:** The hub counts an approval only from a credential that created no version of the change, so the token that works must never be the token that approves.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] IF a configured token is not of the form `parley_pat_<token_id>_<secret>`, or the worker token and the approver token are the same string, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `credentials` without sending either token to the hub
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `credentials: worker token is not a personal access token`, `credentials: approver token is not a personal access token` or `credentials: worker and approver are the same token`; the fake hub saw no request under /api/v1
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding two tokens with the scopes the PRD names; each case changes one thing
   ```
   new file internal/daemon/credentials_test.go, one table for every way the credentials check fails; these rows: {worker = an API key 'parley_ab_cd', approver = 'parley_admin_…', worker == approver}: err = daemon.CheckCredentials(ctx, hubClient, worker, approver); assert err.Error() == the expected reason; assert fake hub request count == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the hub answers a request carrying the worker token or the approver token with 401, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `credentials`
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `credentials: worker token: 401 unauthenticated` or `credentials: approver token: 401 unauthenticated`
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.3] IF the hub answers the worker token's read of its own Token object with `403 token_bound`, or the Token object's `workspace` is not null, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `credentials`
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `credentials: worker token is bound to a workspace`
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.4] IF the `permissions` of the worker token hold `changes:approve`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `credentials`
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `credentials: worker token must not hold changes:approve`
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.5] IF the `permissions` of the worker token lack, by exact name, one of `workspaces:write`, `git:write`, `git:read`, `changes:write`, `checks:write`, `tokens:manage`, `forge:write`, `sessions:write`, `audit:read`, or those of the approver token lack `changes:read` or `changes:approve`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL fail the start check `credentials`, naming the first missing scope in the order given here, the worker token's before the approver token's
   → exit code 1; one line on stderr: `credentials: worker token lacks <scope>` or `credentials: approver token lacks <scope>`; a worker token the hub answers `403 insufficient_scope` when it reads its Token object is reported as `credentials: worker token lacks tokens:manage`
   Check: same as REQ-2.1
1. [REQ-2.6] WHEN both tokens are personal access tokens, differ, are accepted by the hub, and hold the scopes named in REQ-2.5 with the worker token unbound and without `changes:approve`, THE nightshiftd SHALL pass the start check `credentials`, having read both tokens' `permissions` with the worker token from `GET /api/v1/user/tokens/{token_id}` and having taken any answer but 401 to the approver token's own request on that route as its acceptance
   → the check returns no error; the approver token was sent in exactly one request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/daemon/credentials_test.go: err = daemon.CheckCredentials(ctx, hubClient, worker, approver) against the fake hub's two good tokens; assert err == nil; assert the fake hub saw one request bearing the approver token and answered it 403 insufficient_scope
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] WHEN the hub answers 401 to a request carrying the worker token or the approver token while nightshiftd is running, THE nightshiftd SHALL keep running, record the credential error `worker token: 401 unauthenticated` or `approver token: 401 unauthenticated`, and from then on answer "not available" to every part of nightshift that asks whether the hub can be used with that token
   → `GET /api/v1/status` answers `hub.credential_error` with the recorded text; the hub client's availability for that token is false; the process has not exited
   Check: integration
   - setup: a daemon started in-process against a fake hub; after the start the fake hub revokes the worker token
   ```
   new file internal/daemon/lifecycle_test.go: hubClient.Do(any request as worker) -> 401; assert hub.Available(worker) == false; assert hub.Available(approver) == true; assert get('/api/v1/status').json.hub.credential_error == 'worker token: 401 unauthenticated'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.8] WHEN nightshiftd receives SIGHUP, THE nightshiftd SHALL read `hub.worker_token` and `hub.approver_token` from the configuration file again and run the `credentials` check on them; where it passes, use them for every later hub request and clear the credential error; where it fails or the file cannot be loaded, keep the tokens in use and write one line `credentials: <reason>` or `config: <reason>` to its log on stderr
   → after a passing reload `GET /api/v1/status` answers `hub.credential_error: null` and the next hub request carries the new token; after a failing one the next hub request carries the previous token and the process has not exited
   Check: integration
   - setup: the daemon of REQ-2.7 with its worker token revoked; the reload is triggered through the function the SIGHUP handler calls
   ```
   in internal/daemon/lifecycle_test.go, a table over {config rewritten with a new good worker token -> credential_error null and the fake hub's next request bears the new token, config rewritten with worker == approver -> log line 'credentials: worker and approver are the same token' and the next request bears the old token}; plus one case sending a real SIGHUP to a daemon run as a subprocess of the test binary and asserting the reload happened
   ```

### REQ-3: The client token and the API envelope

**Rationale:** The API can start work and answer decisions, so only the person who can read the daemon's files may call it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN nightshiftd starts and no file exists at `token_file`, THE nightshiftd SHALL write a client token of 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, from 32 bytes of the operating system's random source, to that file with mode 0600, creating its parent directory with mode 0700 where it does not exist
   → the file holds the token and a trailing newline; its mode is 0600; two first starts in different directories produce different tokens
   Check: unit
   ```
   new file internal/api/token_test.go: tok = api.EnsureClientToken(path); assert tok matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$; assert stat(path).mode == 0600; assert read(path) == tok + '\n'; assert EnsureClientToken(otherPath) != tok
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN nightshiftd starts and a file exists at `token_file`, THE nightshiftd SHALL use the token the file holds and leave the file unchanged
   → the file's content and modification time are as before the start; requests bearing that token are accepted
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/api/token_test.go: first = EnsureClientToken(path); mtime = stat(path).mtime; second = EnsureClientToken(path); assert second == first; assert stat(path).mtime == mtime
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF a request to any path under `/api/v1` carries no `Authorization: Bearer` header, or carries a value other than the client token, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL reject the request before looking at its route, comparing the token in constant time
   → status 401 with body `{"error_type": "unauthorized", "message": <string>}`; no handler ran; the same answer for an existing route and for a path that names none
   Check: unit
   ```
   new file internal/api/server_test.go, through the router, a table over {no header, 'Bearer wrong', 'Basic <token>', token in a query parameter} x {'/api/v1/status', '/api/v1/nope'}: r = do(req); assert r.status == 401; assert r.json.error_type == 'unauthorized'; assert r.json.message != ''
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any request it answers with a 4xx or 5xx status, send `Content-Type: application/json` and a body `{"error_type", "message"}`, with `404` and `not_found` for an authenticated request whose path names no route, `405` and `method_not_allowed` for one whose route lacks the method, and `500` and `internal` for a handler that panicked
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/api/server_test.go, a table over {GET /api/v1/nope -> 404 not_found, POST /api/v1/status -> 405 method_not_allowed, a test route whose handler panics -> 500 internal}, each with the client token: assert r.status; assert r.header['Content-Type'] starts with 'application/json'; assert r.json.error_type == want; assert r.json.message != ''; assert the server answers the next request after the panic
   ```

### REQ-4: Status and the client's base

**Rationale:** The first thing a person asks a daemon is whether it runs and whether it reaches the hub.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/status`, THE nightshiftd SHALL report the daemon's version, the hub's endpoint, whether the hub is reachable with the time of the first failure when it is not, the credential error when there is one, the running sessions and the workspaces
   → status 200 with body `{"version": string, "hub": {"endpoint": string, "reachable": bool, "unreachable_since": RFC 3339 string or null, "credential_error": string or null}, "sessions": [], "workspaces": []}`; `sessions` and `workspaces` are empty lists while no other package registered a source for them; no token value appears in the body
   Check: unit
   - setup: a server over a hub monitor stub in the state reachable
   ```
   in internal/api/server_test.go: r = get('/api/v1/status'); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.version == buildinfo.Version; assert r.json.hub == {endpoint: cfg endpoint, reachable: true, unreachable_since: null, credential_error: null}; assert r.json.sessions == []; assert r.json.workspaces == []; assert r.body contains neither token
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN the person runs `nightshift status`, THE nightshift SHALL request `GET /api/v1/status` with the client token and print `nightshiftd <version>` and then `hub: <endpoint> reachable`, or `hub: unreachable since <time>` while the hub is unreachable, followed by one line with the credential error when there is one; with `--json`, print the response body instead
   → exit code 0; the lines on stdout; with `--json` stdout parses as the JSON the API answered
   Check: unit
   - setup: an httptest server standing in for the daemon, answering a fixed status document
   ```
   new file internal/cli/cli_test.go, a table over {reachable -> second line 'hub: https://hub.example reachable', unreachable since T -> 'hub: unreachable since ' + T, credential_error set -> third line equals it, --json -> stdout parses to the served document}: code, stdout, stderr = cli.Run(['status', …], env); assert code == 0; assert stdout
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] THE nightshift SHALL for any command, send its requests to the address `--addr` gives, else to `$NIGHTSHIFT_ADDR`, else to `127.0.0.1:7878`, bearing the token read from the file `--token-file` names, else from `~/.nightshift/token`
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/cli_test.go, a table over {--addr and env both set -> the flag's server got the request, env only -> the env's server, neither -> the resolved address is '127.0.0.1:7878'} and {--token-file -> that file's token is the bearer, absent -> <home>/.nightshift/token}: assert the httptest server saw 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] IF the daemon cannot be reached at the address, or the client token file cannot be read, THEN THE nightshift SHALL end the command without output on stdout
   → exit code 1; stderr is `cannot reach nightshiftd at <address>` or `cannot read the client token at <path>`; stdout is empty
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/cli_test.go, a table over {--addr of a closed listener -> 'cannot reach nightshiftd at <addr>', --token-file naming no file -> 'cannot read the client token at <path>'}: code, stdout, stderr = cli.Run(['status', …]); assert code == 1; assert stderr == want + '\n'; assert stdout == ''
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] IF the daemon answers a command's request with a 4xx or 5xx status, THEN THE nightshift SHALL end the command, printing the `message` of the error body
   → exit code 1; stderr is the error's `message`; stdout is empty, or with `--json` holds the error body
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/cli_test.go: the httptest server answers 401 {error_type: 'unauthorized', message: 'the client token is missing or wrong'}; code, stdout, stderr = cli.Run(['status']); assert code == 1; assert stderr == 'the client token is missing or wrong\n'; assert stdout == ''; with --json assert stdout parses to the error body
   ```
1. [REQ-4.6] IF the command line names no command, an unknown command, an unknown flag, or lacks a required argument, THEN THE nightshift SHALL print the usage of the command, or of `nightshift` when none was recognised, and send no request
   → exit code 2; the usage on stderr; stdout is empty; the daemon received no request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/cli_test.go, a table over {[], ['frobnicate'], ['status', '--nope'], ['status', 'extra']}: code, stdout, stderr = cli.Run(args); assert code == 2; assert stderr contains 'usage: nightshift'; assert stdout == ''; assert the httptest server saw no request
   ```

### REQ-5: The event stream

**Rationale:** A thin client that was offline must be able to catch up exactly, or it has to read everything again.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any event appended to the event log, give it a `seq` one greater than the seq of the event appended before it, starting at 1, and a `time`, and write it to the store before any client receives it
   → the append returns the event with its `seq`; appends from concurrent callers yield seqs without a gap or a repeat
   Check: unit
   - setup: an event log over a store in a temporary directory
   ```
   new file internal/event/log_test.go: 8 goroutines each Append 50 events; assert the set of returned seqs == 1..400; assert log.After(0) returns 400 events in seq order with type and data as appended
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/events` without a `Last-Event-ID` header, THE nightshiftd SHALL answer with a server-sent event stream that stays open and carries every event appended after the request, in seq order, each as the lines `id: <seq>`, `event: <type>` and `data: <JSON>` followed by an empty line
   → status 200 with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`; the `data` JSON is `{"seq", "time", "type", "data"}`; an event appended before the request is not sent
   Check: integration
   - setup: an API server over a real event log and store; one event appended before the client connects
   ```
   new file internal/api/events_test.go: s = openStream('/api/v1/events'); assert s.header['Content-Type'] starts with 'text/event-stream'; log.Append(type 'test.a'), log.Append(type 'test.b'); assert s.next() == {id: '2', event: 'test.a', data.seq: 2}; assert s.next().id == '3'
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/events` with `Last-Event-ID: <seq>` and every event after that seq is still kept, THE nightshiftd SHALL send every kept event with a greater seq in order, then every event appended afterwards, sending no event twice and leaving none out, also for events appended while the kept ones are being sent
   → the ids the client receives are seq+1, seq+2, … without a gap or a repeat; `Last-Event-ID` equal to the newest seq yields only later events
   Check: integration
   - setup: a log holding events 1 to 200
   ```
   in internal/api/events_test.go: s = openStream with Last-Event-ID 150 while another goroutine appends 100 events; assert the first 150 ids received == 151..300 in order; a second stream with Last-Event-ID 300 receives nothing until event 301 is appended, then id 301
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] IF a request to `GET /api/v1/events` carries a `Last-Event-ID` and an event with a greater seq has been removed from the log, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the stream
   → status 410 with body `{"error_type": "cursor_expired", "message": <string>, "oldest_seq": <the seq of the oldest kept event, or the next seq to be given when none is kept>}`; no event is sent
   Check: integration
   - setup: a log whose events 1 to 10 were removed and whose events 11 to 20 are kept
   ```
   in internal/api/events_test.go, a table over Last-Event-ID {0, 9 -> 410 cursor_expired with oldest_seq 11; 10 -> 200 and first id 11}: r = get with the header; assert r.status and r.json
   ```
1. [REQ-5.5] IF a request to `GET /api/v1/events` carries a `Last-Event-ID` that is not a non-negative decimal integer, or is greater than the newest seq ever given, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the stream
   → status 400 with body `{"error_type": "invalid_request", "message": <string>}`; no event is sent
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/api/events_test.go, a table over Last-Event-ID {'abc', '-1', '1.5', '', newest+1}: r = get with the header; assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error_type == 'invalid_request'
   ```
1. [REQ-5.6] THE nightshiftd SHALL remove from the event log every event whose `time` is more than 7 days in the past, at start and once an hour after it, and keep every younger event
   Check: unit
   - setup: an event log with an injected clock; events appended at day 0, day 3 and day 8
   ```
   in internal/event/log_test.go: clock = day 8 plus one minute; log.Prune(); assert log.After(0) fails with the cursor-expired error carrying oldest seq of the day-3 event; assert the day-3 and day-8 events are returned by After(seq of the day-0 event); assert the next Append gets the seq after the day-8 event's
   ```
1. [REQ-5.7] THE nightshiftd SHALL for any restart of nightshiftd, keep every event younger than 7 days and continue `seq` from the highest value ever given, also when the event that carried it has been removed
   Check: integration
   - setup: a store file in a temporary directory, opened, used, closed and opened again
   ```
   in internal/event/log_test.go: append 5 events; close the store; reopen; assert After(2) returns seqs 3,4,5; assert Append returns seq 6. Second case: append 3, prune all with the clock moved 8 days, close, reopen; assert Append returns seq 4
   ```
1. [REQ-5.8] IF 256 events wait to be sent to one client of the event stream because it does not read them, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL close that client's connection and release what it held
   → the client's stream ends; appends and every other client's stream go on without delay: an append returns within 100 milliseconds while the stalled client is connected; the stalled client's subscription is gone from the log
   Check: integration
   - setup: two subscribers of a real event log: one reads, one never reads
   ```
   in internal/event/log_test.go: append 300 events, timing each; assert every Append took < 100ms; assert the reading subscriber received 300; assert the stalled subscriber's channel is closed and log.Subscribers() == 1
   ```

### REQ-6: Stopping and the hub's outages

**Rationale:** The daemon runs for weeks; the hub and the machine under it do not stay up that long.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN nightshiftd receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, THE nightshiftd SHALL stop accepting API requests, end every open event stream, run each registered shutdown step with a context that is cancelled 25 seconds after the signal, close the store, and exit
   → exit code 0 within 30 seconds of the signal; a request after the signal is refused at the connection; every registered step was called once; the store file opens cleanly afterwards
   Check: integration
   - setup: a daemon started in-process against a fake hub, with one registered shutdown step and one open event stream
   ```
   in internal/daemon/lifecycle_test.go, a table over {SIGTERM, SIGINT} delivered through the channel the signal handler feeds: code = wait(daemon); assert code == 0; assert the step ran once; assert the stream ended; assert a new request fails to connect; assert store.Open(path) succeeds
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] IF a registered shutdown step has not returned when its context is cancelled, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL abandon the step, close the store and exit
   → exit code 0 no later than 30 seconds after the signal; one line on stderr names the abandoned step
   Check: integration
   - setup: the step deadline and the exit deadline are parameters, set to 100 and 200 milliseconds in the test; one registered step named 'stuck' blocks forever
   ```
   in internal/daemon/lifecycle_test.go: signal the daemon; code = wait(daemon); assert code == 0; assert elapsed < 200ms; assert stderr contains 'stuck'
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] WHEN a request to the hub fails with a connection error or a timeout while the hub is marked reachable, THE nightshiftd SHALL mark the hub unreachable, record the time of that failure as the time of the first failure, and keep running
   → `GET /api/v1/status` answers `hub.reachable: false` and `hub.unreachable_since` equal to the recorded time; a later failed request or probe leaves `unreachable_since` unchanged; the hub client's availability is false for both tokens
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub monitor with an injected clock over a fake hub that is closed
   ```
   new file internal/hub/monitor_test.go: hubClient.Do(request) -> connection error at T0; assert monitor.Reachable() == false; assert monitor.Since() == T0; clock = T0+40s; monitor.Probe() fails; assert monitor.Since() == T0; assert hub.Available(worker) == false
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] WHILE the hub is marked unreachable, THE nightshiftd SHALL request `GET /readyz` of the hub every 30 seconds, and mark the hub reachable, clearing the time of the first failure, at the first answer with status 200
   → after the 200 answer `GET /api/v1/status` reports `hub.reachable: true` and `hub.unreachable_since: null` without a restart; a 503 answer leaves the hub unreachable; no probe is sent while the hub is reachable
   Check: unit
   - setup: a hub monitor whose probe interval is a parameter, set to 10 milliseconds; a fake hub whose /readyz answers 503 three times and then 200
   ```
   in internal/hub/monitor_test.go: mark unreachable; wait until monitor.Reachable(); assert the fake hub saw 4 /readyz requests; assert monitor.Since() is zero; wait 50ms; assert the fake hub saw no further /readyz request; assert the default interval constant is 30 seconds
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A first start and a status query

1. **person** writes a configuration file with the hub's endpoint and the two tokens and starts `nightshiftd --config <file>`
2. **nightshiftd** loads the configuration and requests the hub's `/readyz`
3. **hub** answers `/readyz` with 200 and the token reads with both tokens' permissions
4. **nightshiftd** passes the three start checks, opens the store, writes the client token file and listens
5. **person** runs `nightshift status`
6. **nightshift** reads the client token, requests `GET /api/v1/status` and prints the version and `hub: <endpoint> reachable`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd program's run function with its configuration loader, start checks, store on disk and HTTP listener, the nightshift client's run function, the client token file

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub (internal/hubtest) holding a worker and an approver token with the scopes the PRD names
- a temporary directory for the configuration, the token file and the store
- listen = 127.0.0.1:0, the bound address read back from the daemon

**End state:**

- `nightshift status` exits 0 and prints `nightshiftd <version>` and `hub: <fake hub URL> reachable`
- the token file exists with mode 0600 and the store file exists
- the same request without the token is answered 401 unauthorized

**Pseudocode:**

```
new file internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d = startDaemon(configFile); code, out, _ = cli.Run(['status', '--addr', d.addr, '--token-file', tokenFile]); assert code == 0; assert out == 'nightshiftd ' + version + '\nhub: ' + hubURL + ' reachable\n'; assert stat(tokenFile).mode == 0600; assert rawGet(d.addr + '/api/v1/status').status == 401
```

### PATH-2: A client resumes the event stream after a restart

1. **nightshift** connects to `GET /api/v1/events` and receives events up to a seq
2. **person** sends SIGTERM to nightshiftd
3. **nightshiftd** ends the stream, closes the store and exits with code 0
4. **person** starts nightshiftd again
5. **nightshiftd** opens the same store and appends further events with seqs continuing from the last one
6. **nightshift** reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` set to its last seq and receives every event after it

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function, started twice over one store file, the event log and its store, the HTTP event stream

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub
- events are appended through the event log's append function, the one later packages call, since this package produces none itself

**End state:**

- the first daemon exited with code 0
- the reconnected stream delivers exactly the events appended after the client's last seq, in order, with seqs continuing from before the restart
- a reconnect with a seq whose successor was removed is answered 410 cursor_expired

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d1 = startDaemon(cfg); s = stream(d1); d1.log.Append x3; assert s received ids 1,2,3; d1.signal(SIGTERM); assert d1.wait() == 0; d2 = startDaemon(cfg); d2.log.Append x2; s2 = stream(d2, lastEventID 3); assert s2 received ids 4,5
```

### PATH-3: The hub goes away and comes back

1. **hub** stops answering
2. **nightshiftd** fails a hub request, marks the hub unreachable and records the time
3. **person** runs `nightshift status` and reads `hub: unreachable since <time>`
4. **hub** answers again
5. **nightshiftd** probes `/readyz`, receives 200 and marks the hub reachable
6. **person** runs `nightshift status` and reads `hub: <endpoint> reachable`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with the hub client and its monitor, the HTTP API, the nightshift client's run function

**Setup:**

- a fake Parley hub that can be stopped and started on the same address
- the probe interval set to 20 milliseconds

**End state:**

- while the fake hub is down `nightshift status` prints `hub: unreachable since <time>` and exits 0
- after the fake hub is back `nightshift status` prints `hub: <endpoint> reachable`
- the daemon process was the same throughout

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: d = startDaemon(cfg, probe 20ms); fakeHub.Stop(); d.hub.Do(any request) fails; assert cli status second line starts with 'hub: unreachable since '; fakeHub.Start(); eventually cli status second line == 'hub: ' + hubURL + ' reachable'
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `go vet ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/config/... ./internal/store/... ./internal/hub/... ./internal/daemon/... ./internal/api/... ./internal/event/... ./internal/cli/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

None: this spec depends on no other spec.

## Tasks

### 1. Create the module and load the configuration (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.1, REQ-1.2, REQ-1.3

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Create the Go module github.com/agent-fox-dev/nightshift (Go 1.27) with the two programs cmd/nightshiftd and cmd/nightshift, each a main that only calls a run function taking the arguments, the environment and the output streams and returning the exit code (internal/daemon.Run and internal/cli.Run), so that tests run them in-process
- 1.2 Add a Makefile with the targets build, test (the all_tests command), lint (the linter command), check (gofmt check, lint, then test) and doc (go doc -all of every package outside internal/ into docs/generated/, one text file per package; with none yet, it writes nothing and succeeds)
- 1.3 Add internal/buildinfo with a Version string that is `dev` unless set at link time, and have `make build` set it
- 1.4 Add the configuration behaviours to internal/config/config_test.go and confirm they fail
- 1.5 Add internal/config: Load(path, home) decodes the TOML file with github.com/BurntSushi/toml into the keys listen, token_file, [store].path and [hub].endpoint, worker_token, approver_token, applies the three defaults, expands a leading ~/ against the home directory it is given, and returns an error whose text is the reason alone (the caller adds the `config: ` prefix)
- 1.6 Refuse an unknown key with `unknown key "<dotted key>"`, using the decoder's list of undecoded keys, and a missing required key with `<dotted key> is not set`; later packages add their own keys to the same struct

Test that a store opened, closed and opened again keeps a row, in internal/store/store_test.go

### 2. Check the hub and the two credentials at start (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.4, REQ-1.5, REQ-2.1, REQ-2.2, REQ-2.3, REQ-2.4, REQ-2.5, REQ-2.6

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add internal/hubtest, the fake Parley hub every package's tests use: an httptest server with a scriptable /readyz, a set of personal access tokens with permissions, binding and a revoked flag, the route GET /api/v1/user/tokens/{token_id} answering as Parley does (401 unauthenticated, then 403 token_bound, then 403 insufficient_scope without tokens:read or tokens:manage, 404 for another user's or an unknown id, Parley's error envelope), a log of the requests it saw with their bearer, and Stop and Start on the same address
- 2.2 Add the credential and start-check behaviours to internal/daemon/credentials_test.go and internal/daemon/start_test.go and confirm they fail
- 2.3 Add internal/hub: a client over the endpoint that sends a request with a named credential (worker or approver), decodes Parley's error envelope into an error carrying the status and the error_type, and has Ready(ctx) for GET /readyz and Token(ctx, credential, tokenID) for the Token object
- 2.4 Add the `hub` start check: Ready with a 10 second timeout that is a parameter; map a refused connection, another status and a timeout to the three reasons
- 2.5 Add CheckCredentials: first the form of both tokens and their inequality, with no request; then the worker token reads its own Token object and the approver's, and the approver token sends one request on that route whose 401 alone fails it
- 2.6 Report the reasons in this precedence: not a personal access token, same token, 401 of the worker, 401 of the approver, worker bound, worker lacks tokens:manage (its read was answered insufficient_scope), worker holds changes:approve, first missing worker scope in the PRD's order, first missing approver scope
- 2.7 Have daemon.Run run the checks in the order config, hub, credentials through one ordered list that a later package can append a check to, print `<check>: <reason>` for the first failure and return 1 without running the rest
- 2.8 Name internal/hubtest under Repository Specifics in .specs/steering.md

### 3. Serve the authenticated API with the status, and add the client (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.6, REQ-1.7, REQ-3, REQ-4

### 4. Keep the event log and serve it as a resumable stream (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Depends on:** 3

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the event log behaviours to internal/event/log_test.go and the stream behaviours to internal/api/events_test.go and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add internal/event with its store migration: a table of events (seq, time, type, data as JSON) and a one-row table holding the highest seq ever given, so that seq never goes back after a prune or a restart
- 4.3 Add Append(type, data): give the next seq and the time from an injected clock and write the event and the counter in one transaction, under one lock so that seqs are gapless, then hand the event to every subscriber without blocking
- 4.4 Add After(seq): the kept events with a greater seq in order, a cursor-expired error carrying the oldest kept seq (or the next seq to be given when none is kept) when an event after seq was removed, and an invalid error when seq is greater than the highest ever given
- 4.5 Add Subscribe(afterSeq): register the subscriber under the append lock, replay the kept events after afterSeq and then deliver live ones through a buffer of 256 events, so that none is missed or sent twice; when the buffer is full, close the subscriber's channel and remove it instead of waiting
- 4.6 Add Prune: delete every event older than 7 days by the injected clock; run it when the daemon starts and once an hour from a goroutine that stops with the daemon
- 4.7 Add GET /api/v1/events: validate Last-Event-ID (400 invalid_request), answer 410 cursor_expired with oldest_seq, otherwise stream `id`, `event` and `data` lines with a flush after each event, without Last-Event-ID from the present; end the stream when the client goes away, the subscriber was dropped or the server shuts down
- 4.8 Create the log in daemon.Run over the opened store and expose it to the packages that will append to it
- 4.9 Describe the stream, the cursor, the 7 days and the two refusals in docs/api.md

### 5. Stop on a signal, ride out a hub outage and reload the credentials (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2.7, REQ-2.8, REQ-6

**Depends on:** 3, 4

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the monitor behaviours to internal/hub/monitor_test.go and the lifecycle behaviours to internal/daemon/lifecycle_test.go and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Add the hub monitor in internal/hub: every request the client sends reports its outcome; a connection error or a timeout marks the hub unreachable and records the time of the first failure from an injected clock, which later failures leave unchanged
- 5.3 While unreachable, probe GET /readyz at an interval that is a parameter with the default 30 seconds; the first 200 marks the hub reachable and clears the time; send no probe while reachable; stop with the daemon
- 5.4 Record a 401 answer to a request with the worker or the approver token as that token's credential error (`worker token: 401 unauthenticated`), without marking the hub unreachable for the other token
- 5.5 Add Available(credential): false while the hub is unreachable or that credential has an error; it is what later packages ask before they start a session or land
- 5.6 Feed the monitor's state into GET /api/v1/status in place of the stub
- 5.7 Hold the two tokens behind a lock in the hub client; on SIGHUP load the configuration again, run CheckCredentials on its tokens, swap them in and clear the credential errors when it passes, and write `config: <reason>` or `credentials: <reason>` to stderr and keep the old ones when it does not
- 5.8 On SIGTERM or SIGINT stop the listener, end the event streams, run the registered shutdown steps in registration order with a context cancelled after a deadline that is a parameter with the default 25 seconds, name an abandoned step on stderr, close the store and return 0, no later than an exit deadline with the default 30 seconds
- 5.9 Add a function by which a later package registers a named shutdown step
- 5.10 Add the restart flow and the outage flow to internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, and one test that sends real SIGHUP and SIGTERM to the test binary re-executed as the daemon
- 5.11 Create docs/architecture.md: the two programs, the packages internal/config, store, hub, daemon, api, event and cli, the start sequence and the extension points later packages use (start checks, routes, commands, status sources, migrations, shutdown steps, the event log); add signals and the outage behaviour to docs/cli.md; run `make doc`
